blocks.title: Why Build an Evaluation Harness with promptfoo matters here

spans.text: Problem statement: A policy-answering bot changed prompts and the team needs to catch regressions before release. The learner's job is not to memorize Build an Evaluation Harness with promptfoo; it is to decide what to build or change, what evidence the system may use, and how to tell whether the change improved regression failures caught before deployment.

Running case: Promptfoo-style eval suite with golden cases and assertions. We will keep this same case through the lesson so each idea has a job: frame the problem, explain the mechanism, choose a design, test the implementation, and decide what to do next.

Before reading on, predict: if a prompt update improves tone but drops required policy citations, where would you look first - the input, the state or data, the model boundary, the validation check, or the release process?
The lesson assumes you can learn the vocabulary, then spends its effort on integration choices, failure signals, and checks that make the idea usable in a real system.

items.text: Product framing: Build an Evaluation Harness with promptfoo matters when it changes a user-visible decision, release gate, or operational workflow.
Engineering framing: Build an Evaluation Harness with promptfoo matters when it changes data, state, prompts, model behavior, tools, schemas, traces, or runtime constraints.
Validation framing: the lesson is not complete until the team can measure regression failures caught before deployment on examples that resemble the real workload.

Here is the worked artifact at design-review depth: concrete enough to inspect, small enough to build as a thin slice.
Complete worked artifact

items.text: Release change: a prompt or workflow update makes answers warmer, but the team must prove it did not lose required facts, citations, refusals, or safe tool behavior.

Artifact: Promptfoo-style eval suite with golden cases and assertions. It includes golden inputs, expected behaviors, assertions, failure labels, owner, and the release gate for regression failures caught before deployment.
Worked output: case refund-policy-1 must include "30 days" and "invoice id", must not promise guaranteed approval, and must cite the refund policy source.

blocks.title: Case study: what changed after the first review

spans.text: The first prototype works on the demo path. Then a reviewer runs the uncomfortable case: a prompt update improves tone but drops required policy citations. The output still looks confident, which is exactly why the lesson needs a richer artifact.

The team does not restart from scratch. It adds one missing control to Promptfoo-style eval suite with golden cases and assertions: a stricter input contract, better source metadata, a validation assertion, a human-review edge, a rollback trigger, or an audit log depending on where the failure appeared.

items.text: Decision made: keep the thin slice, but block release until the failure is observable and repeatable.
Evidence added: the artifact now shows the input, intermediate evidence, final output, and pass/fail reason.
Metric promoted: regression failures caught before deployment becomes part of the release gate instead of a dashboard someone checks later.

spans.text: Case-study takeaway: a useful Build an Evaluation Harness with promptfoo design makes the wrong answer inspectable before it reaches users.
